The diagnostic that says do not build

Sometimes the strongest technology recommendation is to stop before capital is committed.

Illustrative scenario analysis · 6–8 minute read
This article illustrates a recurring supply-chain pattern and the JourneyIQ Supply Chain Diagnostic method. It does not describe a named client, completed engagement or verified customer outcome.

Start with the decision

Perform the analysis manually on a bounded dataset and test whether it creates a decision the customer values.

Four tests before a build

Test access, novelty, actionability and repeatability—not only whether stakeholders like a prototype.

Reasons to stop

Stop if the data cannot be accessed, findings are already obvious, transformation remains bespoke or recurring demand is weak.

What earns the right to build

Automate only when the same journey, definitions and decision pattern repeat often enough to create genuine value.
